headlines: mandapa scope: the title and section 7 say 'the block's memory' but the body says nirmmita's; a mala made inside a block is NEVER given back (persistent allocation via emit_nirmmita_from_rax -> r65_emit_nirm, no scratch path) and its address can leave freely with no refusal (no taint for mala names in r73_taint) - the chapter never mentions a mala

E_SCRATCH_ESCAPE: the chapter names two refused shapes; the code refuses three (store into memory via r73_fail_mem unmentioned) while the blanket 'may not leave' overstates it (ordinary call arguments are never checked)
agrim (continue) also rewinds via r73_wrap_jump and is never named - 'however it ends' lists three endings, there are four
the budget counts aligned bytes: nirmmita(1000) costs 1008, so parimita 1000 + one nirmmita(1000) is refused; nested budgets count against every budgeted block around them
N must be positive (zero/negative is a compile error) and 'parimita = N' is silently no budget at all
'baait' (bytes) is never defined anywhere in the chapter or the reference
parimana() counts a mala too, and a kosh made inside a block costs more (56-byte header with R82 vs 32)

slice bounds ARE checked at runtime with a message naming 'mala' (mala ank seema atikram for a kosh slice); the chapter says nothing about bounds or about k[lo:], k[:hi], mala slices, slices of slices, or the kosh-dasham refusal
kosh CREATION failure has its own message (kosh rachayitum smritih na labdha, :709), never shown; section 6 covers only growth
nirmmita failure returns 0 - no sentence, no stop ('nirmmita promises 0 on failure', :26784-26785); the program continues and crashes on first use, undercutting section 7's 'not a crash'
kshetra purnam is named once, never explained (scratch-side out-of-memory); the budget check fires before it
'you can see where memory is held' over-promises - parimana() tells how much, not where; no introspection exists
a whole mala can be passed to a vibhag parameter and a kosh dasham cannot - neither mentioned
writes are bounds-checked too, unmentioned (TRUE for reads, INCOMPLETE)
implied_features: the section 2 title and section 7 imply block reclamation applies to all memory made inside a block (it does not - a kosh keeps its bytes, a mala is never given back)
'you can see where memory is held' implies introspection that does not exist
by omission, sections 6-7 imply every memory failure stops with a sentence (a nirmmita failure does not)
